heading: Congressional findings and declaration of purpose

tree.heading: Rights and liabilities undefined
tree.text: The Congress finds that the use of electronic systems to transfer funds provides the potential for substantial benefits to consumers. However, due to the unique characteristics of such systems, the application of existing consumer protection legislation is unclear, leaving the rights and liabilities of consumers, financial institutions, and intermediaries in electronic fund transfers undefined.

tree.heading: Purposes
tree.text: It is the purpose of this subchapter to provide a basic framework establishing the rights, liabilities, and responsibilities of participants in electronic fund and remittance transfer systems. The primary objective of this subchapter, however, is the provision of individual consumer rights.

notes.heading: Amendments
notes.text: 2010—Subsec. (b). Pub. L. 111–203 inserted “and remittance” after “electronic fund”.

notes.heading: Effective Date of 2010 Amendment
notes.text: Amendment by Pub. L. 111–203 effective 1 day after July 21, 2010, except as otherwise provided, see section 4 of Pub. L. 111–203, set out as an Effective Date note under section 5301 of Title 12, Banks and Banking.

notes.heading: Short Title
notes.text: This subchapter known as the “Electronic Fund Transfer Act”, see Short Title note set out under section 1601 of this title.
